c1.note: FY2026 10-K states Walmart uses a global supply chain with U.S. and international suppliers for merchandise sold in stores, clubs and online.

c2.note: No direct passage, but consistent with the 10-K (global supply chain, distribution facilities incl. eCommerce fulfillment centers, stores and clubs); a general characterization.

c3.note: 10-K: in many instances purchases from producers located near stores and clubs, particularly perishables.

c5.note: 10-K risk language ties in-stock levels and assortment to supplier ability, supply chain timing and distribution; the cited passage only covers the supply chain section, but this matches known 10-K wording.

c6.note: 10-K states 192 U.S. distribution facilities as of Jan 31, 2026, using a private truck fleet plus common carriers.

c7.note: 10-K: private truck fleet combined with contracted common carriers.

c8.note: 10-K lists 179 facilities in Africa, Canada, Central America, Chile, China, India and Mexico.

c9.note: 10-K says international facilities process and distribute both imported and domestic products.

c11.note: Footnote (3) says U.S. distribution facilities are used by both Walmart U.S. and Sam's Club U.S.

c12.note: Footnote (1): international properties except Canada are as of Dec 31, 2025; Canada as of Jan 31, 2026.

c13.note: 10-K table covers distribution facilities including eCommerce fulfillment centers and return facilities; footnote (2) notes third-party owned and operated facilities.

c14.note: Counts are consolidated across Walmart U.S., Sam's Club U.S. and International segments, not Walmart U.S. alone.

c15.note: 10-K: for fiscal 2026 the majority of store and club merchandise purchases were shipped through these facilities.

c16.note: 10-K says majority of purchases went through distribution facilities; the 10-K continues that most of the remainder shipped directly from suppliers (consistent with the passage cut-off and 3 systems).

c17.note: Weaker form of the 10-K statement that most of the remainder ships directly from suppliers; some does, so true.

c18.note: 10-K: during fiscal 2026 began combining Sam's Club U.S. supply chain function with Walmart U.S. to streamline operations and leverage enterprise systems.

c19.note: Consistent with the 10-K description of eCommerce fulfillment via stores, clubs, fulfillment centers and other distribution facilities; 5 systems agree.

c20.note: ESG report and press releases give ~280M weekly customers, 10,900+ stores, 19 countries, $713.2B revenue.

c21.note: 10-K shows Walmart U.S. retail units 4,611 at period end (Jan 31, 2026).

c22.note: 10-K: substantially all stores provide same-day pickup and delivery, including in-home delivery.

c23.note: 10-K: pickup and delivery from approximately 3,300 locations across International markets.

c24.note: Walmart press release dated May 26, 2026 announces Prepaid Consolidation supply chain strategy.

c25.note: Press release states the program simplifies inbound supplier logistics, speeds products to shelves and lowers costs.

c27.note: Release: expands first mile capabilities for prepaid suppliers using national network to merge shipments.

c28.note: Release: single national PO to one location, combined and distributed across 42 RDCs.

c29.note: Release names C.H. Robinson, Hub Group, RJW Logistics and a transparent price-per-case rate; 'automated consolidation centers' not visible in the excerpts but likely in the release.

c30.note: Release: scales in phases, participation prioritized by volume alignment and capacity expansion.

c31.note: Press release says the Prepaid Consolidation Program scales in phases and is optional for suppliers, so it does not cover every supplier.

c32.note: Walmart's 10-K describes RDCs as part of the broader U.S. distribution facility network; no passage contradicts this.

c34.note: Oct 29, 2026 release confirms the expanded agreement for 25 U.S. RDCs. Variant F's 'over several years' matches the 8-K's 'number of years' wording, and A's $6B is supported.

c35.note: Release says the agreement supports additional opportunities across Walmart's global supply chain network.

c36.note: The 8-K describes commitments across multiple locations over a number of years; the exact passage was not shown, but this matches the other units' description.

c37.note: Logistics Viewpoints cites the $6 billion headline, and the release says the initial commitment is approximately that amount.

c39.note: 8-K: Walmart committed $125,000,000 to fund R&D of next-generation racking technology and related picking capabilities.

c40.note: Release quotes this wording nearly verbatim.

c41.note: Release says the capabilities help offer a broader assortment, improve speed and provide more reliable replenishment.

c42.note: Walmart release dated Oct 8, 2026 says it opened its fifth next-generation fulfillment center, 900,000+ sq ft, in Stockton.

c43.note: Release confirms a more than 900,000-square-foot facility using advanced automation, technology and machine learning.

c44.note: Release confirms 1,000+ jobs and faster shipping and delivery across California and the West Coast.

c45.note: Release says the technology materially improves storage capacity and daily orders fulfilled versus a traditional fulfillment center.

c47.note: The Oct 8, 2026 release states the 95% reach with next- or two-day shipping.

c48.note: The Nov 5, 2026 release announces a multi-year agreement for 300 Zipline sites with potential to expand.

c49.note: The release says more than 2 million deliveries and that Walmart has worked with Zipline since 2021.

c50.note: The key insights say as fast as 30 minutes and tens of thousands of items via the app or Walmart.com for eligible customers.

c51.note: The release calls Walmart the operator of the nation's largest retail drone delivery program and says 90% of America lives within 10 miles of a Walmart store.

c52.note: The July 2025 Walmart article quotes this wording, though it is about 16 months old.

c53.note: The July 2025 article describes scaling AI/ML across the global supply chain, consistent with the 2026 releases on automation.

c54.note: The article says these systems act as the air traffic control of the supply chain, coordinating fulfillment and optimizing fresh delivery routes to reduce waste and keep food at peak quality.

c55.note: The tools list includes predictive WMS/TMS, the orchestration layer for warehouse controls, enterprise inventory, and agentic AI tools.

c56.note: The tools list defines Self-Healing Inventory in nearly identical words.

c57.note: The tools list covers enterprise inventory, predictive WMS/TMS, self-healing inventory and the orchestration layer for warehouse controls.

c58.note: The Enterprise Inventory entry offers a single, unified view of stock across stores, fulfillment centers and online.

c59.note: Walmart's supplier requirements page covers standards for suppliers, and the claim matches its known sections, though the passages shown don't quote every item.

c61.note: The FY2026 ESG report states that more than 1,000 Associate to Driver graduates moved into Private Fleet roles as of January 2026. It is a workforce side fact and not dated within the last 90 days.

c62.note: Fox Business, April 4, 2023, reports the plan for 65% of stores to be serviced by automated supply chains by 2026. This is an old target, and its fiscal-year end of FY2026 has now passed.

c63.note: The saved excerpts do not show the 55% figure. It matches Walmart's April 2023 investor-meeting target as I recall it, so confidence is medium. The target is dated and the period has ended.

c64.note: The Fox Business subhead says Walmart's automation plans could improve costs per unit by about 20%, which matches the April 2023 target. It is a dated target and no actual result is given.

c33.note: No source was cited and I found no passage that states this. The claim is generic and plausible: Walmart's automation rollout (Symbotic, Stockton next-generation fulfillment center) is phased by facility and market. Confidence is medium.

c46.note: The Walmart Stockton page says the automated, high-density storage and retrieval system brings products directly to associates and cuts the 12-step process to five steps.

c60.note: Walmart's supplier requirements page says its supply chain only works when suppliers pack, label and ship products to the correct specifications.

c16.note: Walmart's fiscal 2026 10-K says most purchases went through its distribution facilities, 'while most of the remaining merchandise we purchased was shipped directly from suppliers to our stores and clubs.' This is the latest 10-K.

c17.note: Same fiscal 2026 10-K passage confirms that some merchandise ships directly from suppliers to stores and clubs.

c42.note: Walmart's Oct. 8, 2026 press release says it opened its fifth next-generation fulfillment center, a facility of more than 900,000 sq ft in Stockton, California.
